dog.description_text: Nelly - 4 years, 19lbs, Chiweenie, Spayed This dog is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application a t socialteesnyc.org Our Team Says: "This pup was rescued from a hoarding situation in PR - involving about 40 dogs. Due to this these pups are on the shyer side and need patient people who will give them time to get used to normal life. They are very sweet dogs: just need more time and patience. We love these dogs - we've rescued about 15 of them and they have all been a joy." Thier Foster Parent Says: "Nelly is the sweetest, gentlest girl with so much love to give! She can be shy and a little hesitant when meeting new people, but once she feels safe and comfortable, her affectionate personality really shines. One of my favorite things about her is how enthusiastically she wags her tail whenever I interact with her at home. Her little tail just keeps going left and right nonstop! She loves attention, gentle pets, and massages, and sometimes she even closes her eyes in complete relaxation while being massaged. She also likes following me around the apartment where she will quietly watch what I'm doing. She is truly a sweet soul who just wants to be loved. Nelly is a professional couch potato! She absolutely loves sleeping and can happily spend hours napping in a cozy spot. She is very calm and peaceful indoors and doesn't need constant entertainment or stimulation. When I leave home, she usually settles down and sleeps peacefully until I return. Once I'm back, she greets me enthusiastically with her adorable wagging tail! She is not an overly energetic or playful dog, and I think that is part of what makes her so special. She is perfectly content just being near her people, enjoying affection, and relaxing in a comfortable environment. Outside, Nelly is a curious little explorer! She loves sniffing everything and taking her time investigating her surroundings. Although she enjoys exploring, she can be nervous around loud noises and sudden movements, particularly when large trucks or bicycles pass by. She is still building her confidence in the outside world, so patience, reassurance, and a gentle approach are important. She isn't the type of dog who needs to run around or play nonstop. She seems happiest enjoying a peaceful walk at her own pace, with plenty of opportunities to sniff. Nelly also gets along very well with my own dog, who came from the same rescue group in Puerto Rico. They coexist beautifully and peacefully at home, often relaxing in separate spots or taking turns enjoying the couch. She has been very respectful of his space, and I've had no issues having them together. In terms of potty training, Nelly is making progress! She consistently poops outside and has also started peeing outdoors more often. However, she sometimes still prefers using a pee pad indoors. She knows exactly where the pee pad is and deliberately goes there when she needs to pee. Her habits are improving, and I believe she will continue making progress with a patient family and a consistent routine. Overall, Nelly is such a special girl. She may not be the most outgoing or playful dog, but she has an incredibly gentle and loving personality. She doesn't ask for much—just a safe, peaceful home, a cozy place to sleep, and someone who will give her the love and affection she deserves. Given her background, it's especially heartwarming to see her slowly discovering how wonderful life with humans can be. I think she would thrive with a patient, loving family who appreciates her calm temperament and gives her the time she needs to build confidence. She has so much love to give, and whoever adopts her will be getting a truly wonderful companion!" Level of dog ownership experience required: BEGINNER – “Beginner” doesn’t necessarily mean easy as all dogs will require time, work, and patience, but we predict this dog will be low on the challenge scale because of their breed/age combo. Potentially a good fit for someone who has relevant dog care experience (fostering, dog sitting) and is looking to adopt their first pup. TOLERANCE TO CITY Adjusting to the city – Spooked easily by loud noises and bustling areas but walks pretty well in quiet areas and probably just needs more time to adjust (may be a puppy or a brand new rescue). POTTY TRAINING Yes — Goes outside and uses pads COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS Wallflower – Very shy with new people and takes a while to warm up. Afraid when unfamiliar people try to say hi on the street, hides or shrinks back when new people visit the home. BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision) Maybe for age 12 and up – Is either big and energetic (okay with kids big enough not to get knocked down) or a little skittish (could be comfortable with older children that can be extra gentle) SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS Yes – Good with most other dogs (sizes, breeds, etc.) as far as we know and enjoys socializing with other canines RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.) Okay to be in a home with a cat MOUTHY BEHAVIOR Past this stage– Little to no interest in chewing on stuff or putting things in their mouth that aren’t food. Doesn’t try to chew on hands, feet, etc. during playtime SEPARATION ANXIETY (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.) Past this stage – Completely fine being left home alone. Doesn’t cry or exhibit destructive behavior when you leave the apartment or house. LEASH MANNERS Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction. CUDDLE BUG LEVEL Lower – Independent, mostly keeps to themself (may be a new rescue or shy, this could change) JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO Calm Greetings – Doesn’t jump up on people or dogs. Always all four on the floor. CRATE TRAINING NELLY - Not at all – Don’t even have one, I’ve puppy proofed and we free range. Medical status: Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake How did this dog end up with Social Tees? Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses. This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes. LEARN MORE ABOUT US: socialteesnyc.org and Instagram @socialteesnyc
